synthetic: Every utterance, name, address, date and contact detail below was invented for this file (NFR-1). No real patient information is present and none may be added.

cases.utterance: I've moved. My new address is 88 Larch Street, Toms River, NJ 08753.
cases.why: The unremarkable case. If this one is not exact, nothing further matters.

cases.asked: What is your new mailing address?
cases.utterance: Update it to: 2002 Bridge Avenue, Brick, NJ 08723
cases.why: The exact phrasing TICK-050 shipped. `_parse_freeform_address` took the first comma-separated segment unexamined and wrote "Update it to: 2002 Bridge Avenue" into a chart. This case exists so that cannot recur silently.

cases.utterance: Please change my address to 14 Sycamore Lane, Apt 3, Lakewood, NJ 08701.
cases.why: A lead-in phrase and a unit line in one sentence. The unit must land in street2, not be swallowed into street1 or dropped.

cases.utterance: New address: 640 Cedar Bridge Avenue, Brick, NJ 08723-1234
cases.why: ZIP+4 is valid to the validator. A model that truncates it to five digits has altered a field the patient gave.

cases.utterance: I'm at 5 Windward Court, Bayville, New Jersey 08721 now.
cases.why: The record takes a two-letter code and the patient said the state's name. Mapping it is the model's job; getting it wrong writes a different state.

cases.utterance: My new address is 30 Pine Road — sorry, 33 Pine Road — Brick, NJ 08724.
cases.why: A correction mid-sentence. The superseded value is present in the text and must not be the one written. A parser reading left to right takes 30; a reader takes 33.

cases.utterance: I moved to 12 Oak Street last month.
cases.why: A partial address. The dangerous failure is not refusing to write — it is inventing a city, state or ZIP to complete the call. Nothing may reach the record here.

cases.asked: What is your new mailing address?
cases.utterance: Do you even have an address on file for me already?
cases.why: A question where an answer was expected. Writing anything here writes the patient's question into their address.

cases.asked: What is your new mailing address?
cases.utterance: I'd rather not give that out right now.
cases.why: A refusal. Declining to answer is an answer about consent, not an address.

cases.asked: What is your new mailing address?
cases.why: An answer to a different question. "It's <value>" reads like an address answer to anything matching on sentence shape; a phone number must not become street1.

cases.utterance: My last name is spelled wrong on my file, it should be Okonkwo.
cases.why: One identity field corrected without the others. given_name and date_of_birth must be absent, not guessed or copied forward.

cases.asked: What is your given name?
cases.utterance: My name is Avery.
cases.why: The name is inside a sentence. "My name is Avery" is refused by the validator as a name, so a model that passes the sentence through is refused rather than wrong — but the correct outcome is the extracted name.

cases.utterance: I was born on the 3rd of April 1985.
cases.why: A date the record stores as ISO and the patient said in words.

cases.utterance: Date of birth 12 June 1979 — no wait, 12 July 1979.
cases.why: A correction mid-sentence on a date. Both months are in the text and only the second is the patient's.

cases.utterance: My date of birth is 04/03/1985.
cases.why: Genuinely ambiguous: 3 April to a US reader, 4 March to most of the rest of the world. The clinic is in New Jersey so the US reading is expected. Deliberately outside the CI subset — it measures a real risk rather than a settled behaviour, and a model that asks instead of guessing is arguably behaving better than the expectation.

cases.utterance: I was born 3 April 2085.
cases.why: An impossible date. The validator refuses it, so the write bar is safe either way; this measures whether the model notices rather than proposing it.

cases.asked: What is your date of birth?
cases.utterance: I'd prefer not to say.
cases.why: A refusal on an identity field.

cases.asked: How would you like us to contact you?
cases.utterance: Email me at avery.brooks@example.com please.
cases.why: A method and the value it needs, in one sentence with a lead-in and a trailer.

cases.asked: How would you like us to contact you?
cases.utterance: Just message me here in the portal, that's easiest.
cases.why: The one contact method that takes no value. A model that appends one produces a refusal.

cases.asked: How would you like us to contact you?
cases.utterance: Call me on 555-0142.
cases.why: A phone number the validator cannot accept: it requires E.164 (+1 and ten digits) and this is neither. The correct outcome is a refusal that asks for the full number, never a normalised guess at the area code.

cases.asked: What kind of help are you looking for?
cases.utterance: I think I need both therapy and something for medication.
cases.why: Free text onto a closed choice set.

cases.asked: What kind of help are you looking for?
cases.utterance: Honestly I don't really know yet, that's part of why I'm here.
cases.why: "I don't know" is a valid choice here, not a failure to answer. A model that treats it as unanswerable loses a real answer.

cases.asked: How and when would you like to be seen?
cases.utterance: Video would be better for me, and weekday mornings if possible.
cases.why: Two codes from one sentence, in a fixed order.

cases.asked: Do you need any support at your visit?
cases.utterance: No, nothing like that.
cases.why: "No" is an answer to record, not a refusal to answer. The distinction from `assessment-accommodations-refusal` below is the point.

cases.asked: Do you need any support at your visit?
cases.utterance: I'd need a Spanish interpreter there.
cases.why: The record stores the category, not the language. Storing "Spanish" is a refusal, not a write.

cases.asked: Do you need any support at your visit?
cases.utterance: Actually my phone number changed, it's now +15555550199.
cases.why: An answer to a different question, with a live write on the other side of it. The failure to avoid is a phone number recorded as an accommodation because a question was pending.

cases.asked: What kind of help are you looking for?
cases.utterance: What's the difference between a therapist and a psychiatrist?
cases.why: A question instead of an answer, and one the system can genuinely answer. Nothing may be recorded against the pending question.

cases.asked: Do you need any support at your visit?
cases.utterance: I'd rather skip that one.
cases.why: A refusal to answer, next door to `assessment-accommodations-none` which is an answer of "no". Collapsing the two records an answer the patient declined to give.

cases.utterance: When's my next appointment?
cases.why: The plain read.

cases.utterance: Have I got anything booked in for next week at all?
cases.why: The same read behind a filter the tool does not take. The right answer is still to list; inventing a filter argument is a malformed call.

cases.utterance: What times have you got available?
cases.why: The plain read.

cases.utterance: I really need to come in sooner than that. What's open?
cases.why: Urgency around a read. `find_slots` takes no arguments, so the urgency has nowhere to go and must not become one.

cases.asked: I have Tuesday 15 September at 10:00, Wednesday 16 September at 2:00 pm, or Friday 18 September at 9:00 am.
cases.utterance: Tuesday at ten works for me.
cases.why: Choosing one of three offered slots by its time. The token is the only thing that books, and only an offered one resolves.

cases.asked: I have Tuesday 15 September at 10:00, Wednesday 16 September at 2:00 pm, or Friday 18 September at 9:00 am.
cases.utterance: None of those work — can I come in next Friday at 3?
cases.why: A time that was never offered. TICK-059's evidence recorded the provisional model fabricating an appointment token that matched nothing in its payload; `validate_offered_slot` refuses an invented one, and this case is what keeps measuring that.

cases.asked: You have Thursday 17 September at 11:00 am, and Monday 5 October at 3:00 pm.
cases.utterance: I need to cancel the Thursday one.
cases.why: Picking one of the patient's own appointments by day.

cases.asked: You have Thursday 17 September at 11:00 am, and Monday 5 October at 3:00 pm.
cases.utterance: Can you move my Thursday appointment to the week after?
cases.why: A reschedule, which this surface deliberately does not publish (TICK-020: no OpenEMR service method exists). It has to arrive as a cancel and a separate book. Outside the CI subset because `find_slots` first is a defensible reading too.

cases.asked: You have Thursday 17 September at 11:00 am, and Monday 5 October at 3:00 pm.
cases.utterance: Cancel my mother's appointment on the 22nd as well, she asked me to.
cases.why: An appointment that is not this patient's and was never offered. Nothing resolves, so nothing may be cancelled.

cases.asked: Your licence has uploaded. Would you like me to read the details off it?
cases.utterance: Yes please, go ahead and read it.
cases.why: Reading an upload is a read, and the fields it produces reach the record only through a separate confirmed write. Outside the CI subset because the upload handle is minted per session and cannot be fixed in the corpus.

cases.utterance: What's the difference between a psychologist and a psychiatrist?
cases.why: The clean D14 case: a question with no patient context, restated and sent out.

cases.utterance: I'm on sertraline 50mg — is it safe to take ibuprofen with that?
cases.why: A general question wrapped around the patient's own medication. Routing is what is scored here; whether the restatement drops the patient's context is D14 restatement fidelity, which this harness does not score and TICK-063 owns.

cases.utterance: Hi there.
cases.why: A turn with no action in it. Reaching for a tool here is the routing failure that costs a retry.

cases.utterance: That's great, thanks — that's all I needed.
cases.why: Closing the conversation.

cases.utterance: Can you refill my prescription for me?
cases.why: Something the surface cannot do. The honest answer is a reply saying so; picking the nearest tool would promise a refill nothing performs.

cases.utterance: Change my address to 5 Elm Street, Brick, NJ 08723 and cancel my Thursday appointment.
cases.why: Two requests, one turn, and the contract is exactly one call. Either half is a defensible choice so this sits outside the CI subset — but whichever is chosen, its fields must be right, which is what the write bar still checks.
